title: Electrical short circuit
summary: An overloaded extension board sparks and starts to smoke. Stay safe around electricity.
sources: National Disaster Management Authority (India): fire safety guidance
Standard electrical safety advice: isolate the supply, never use water on electrical fires

scenes.narration: You're charging a laptop on an extension board crowded with plugs. There's a burning-plastic smell, a crackle, and sparks from the board.

choices.label: That's an electrical fault: danger
choices.feedback: Right. Sparks, crackling and a burning smell mean an electrical fault that can start a fire.

choices.label: It always does that. Ignore it.
choices.feedback: Sparks and burning smells are never normal. Overloaded boards cause many house fires.

scenes.narration: A thin line of smoke rises from the board. The plastic is starting to melt.

choices.label: Switch off the power at the main switch (MCB) if you can reach it safely
choices.feedback: Yes. Cutting the supply at the mains stops the fault feeding the fire.

choices.label: Pull out the plugs from the smoking board
choices.feedback: Don't touch a sparking, melting board: you could get a shock or burn. Isolate at the mains instead.

choices.label: Throw water on it
choices.feedback: Never put water on an electrical fire: water conducts electricity and can electrocute you.

scenes.narration: The power is off, but small flames have caught the curtain next to the board.

choices.label: Get everyone out, close the door, and call 112
choices.feedback: Right. Once it spreads to furnishings, get out and call the fire service.

choices.label: Try to beat out the curtain flames with a towel
choices.feedback: Spreading fires grow fast. Unless you're trained and the fire is tiny, get out and call for help.

choices.label: Use a CO₂ extinguisher only if you've been trained and have a clear way out
choices.feedback: That can be right for a trained person on a very small fire, with the power off and an exit behind you. If in doubt, get out.

end-safe.text: The fire service makes the room safe. Everyone is fine. The electrician later finds the board was badly overloaded.

end-unsafe.text: The curtain fire spread while you fought it. You escape, but with smoke in your lungs. Get out early.

learn: Sparks, crackles and burning smells mean an electrical fault.
Switch off at the main switch (MCB) if you can do it safely; don't touch the faulty item.
Never use water on an electrical fire.
If the fire spreads, get out, close the door and call 112.
disclaimer: Training only. This is not a substitute for emergency services or certified first-aid and fire-safety training. In a real emergency in India, call 112.
